notes: arduino-nano-matter was not in the supplied catalogue list, so it is defined as a new part type with assumed pin names.

The wiring diagram image was not available. The circuit follows the text: driver powered from 3V3, PWM on D4. The photo shows the motor leads going straight to the driver output, and a Grove cable and a green adapter that are not catalogue parts.
The tutorial lists 6 jumper wires, but only 5 connections can be identified, so 5 are used. The 6th is omitted.
The driver port that receives D4 (SDA) is a guess. The Grove module's signal-input pin is not specified.

Breadboard hole positions are assumed. The Nano is taken to straddle the centre gap with 3V3 at column 3, D4 at column 8 and GND at column 13. The Grove driver module is modelled as resting on the breadboard.
Motor-to-wire joints are modelled as soldered or permanent leads. The Nano's other pins are not connected.
